    1. paint(GraphicsContext, CellContext)

Interface CellRenderer

Functional Interface:
This is a functional interface and can therefore be used as the assignment target for a lambda expression or method reference.
@FunctionalInterface public interface CellRenderer

Paints the content of one cell, like Swing's TableCellRenderer, but draws directly instead of returning a component. One instance serves all cells, so it must be stateless.

When it runs, the background and the selection are painted; grid lines, selection outlines and the focus border come after all cells. The GraphicsContext starts in the same state for every cell: font, fill and stroke from the context, text aligned left and centered on its baseline (VPos.CENTER), full opacity, line width 1, no effect. A renderer may change these freely; anything it pushes with save() it must restore().

A renderer that throws is reported once and its cell stays empty; the other cells are still painted.

What costs time

A renderer runs for every visible cell on every frame. Measured with one renderer for all of about 850 cells on screen (1280×800, narrow columns), vsync off, on the laptop the README describes, where the grid itself takes 1.1 ms per frame; RendererBenchmark in the showcase module measures it on any machine:

Drawing in every cell Time per frame
rectangles, lines, ovals, rounded rectangles, an image made once 1.2 ms, as much as nothing
text (fillText, CellRenderers.drawText(GraphicsContext, CellContext, String, HPos)) 1.6 ms
text in three fonts taking turns 1.3 to 1.8 ms
text inside a clip (clip()) 1.7 to 2.2 ms
a triangle (fillPolygon) 2.4 ms
two lines as a path (beginPath, lineTo, stroke) 4 ms
a polyline of 10 points (strokePolyline) 5.5 ms
text with an effect (setEffect(new DropShadow(...))) 34 to 37 ms
a snapshot of a Label, taken per cell 720 ms

The graphics card draws rectangles, lines, ovals, rounded rectangles, images and text. Paths, polygons and polylines are rasterized on the CPU, and an effect renders each cell into a texture of its own. Prefer the first group for anything in every cell: the check box of CellRenderers.BOOLEAN draws its mark as two lines because as one path it doubled the time of a frame. Make colors, fonts and formats once, in fields, rather than per cell.

Nodes in cells

A renderer only paints: the grid is one canvas, not a node per cell, so it cannot hold a Button, a ComboBox or any other node. For the look of a node, draw a picture of it: take node.snapshot(null, null) once per distinct value, keep the images in a map and draw them with gc.drawImage. Drawing a kept image costs nothing measurable; a snapshot per cell and frame makes the grid unusable. For interaction there are other ways: in-place editing (Grid.setEditable(boolean)), the cell action (Grid.setOnCellAction(Consumer)), a cell's context menu (Grid.cellContextMenuFactoryProperty()) and a node in its tooltip (Grid.tooltipGraphicProviderProperty()); a form next to the grid suits anything bigger.
